newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers block Paris Charles de Gaulle airport.
newsitem.headline: Truckers block Paris Charles de Gaulle airport.

text.p: Striking French lorry drivers said that trucking movements in an out of Paris Charles de Gaulle airport had been brought to a standstill since earlier this morning.

"As we speak, no trucks can either leave or enter, while around 150 trucks are blocked in traffic on the A1 motorway close to the airport," a CFDT union official co-ordinating the drivers action told Reuters.
The barricades would be maintained until further notice, the official said.
The lorry drivers are demanding wage hikes, shorter working hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.

Road Flight Systems (RFS), one of France's main road haulage operators specialising in trucked airfreight, said four of its trucks were trapped in traffic while others scheduled to leave CDG, had remained in the depot.
"Normally, Monday is a very busy day for us with around 30 scheduled trucking departures from CDG but at the moment we are at a standstill," an RFS official said

RFS operates a fleet of around 40 trucks from Paris carrying air cargo on behalf of several airlines including Air France, Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific and Air Canada to a number of European gateways.
At Paris-Orly airport, no barricades had been set up and trucks were leaving and arriving as normal, an airport official told Reuters.

A management official at the Paris wholesale market which handles fresh produce - meat ,fish, fruit and vegetables - some of it brought in by truck from CDG and Orly, said there was "no supply problem" despite the blocade of a truck depot nearby.
The drivers action, which began on November 18, has now been extended to 100 road barricades nationwide.

All-night talks, between drivers unions representatives and road hauage bosses, under the auspices of a government mediator, broke up earlier this morning and are set to resume later in the day. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
